question: Does GPT-6 at max effort beat the gateway's default medium effort for framework (FW) chat/completions roles by enough to pay for its reasoning tokens? On li26's frozen 8-K item task this is a cost and wire test with a non-inferiority bound, not a quality ranking.
freeze: Before the first scored call: set status to frozen, rerun `build_r02.py frozen --update-plan` and `build_r02.py subset ... --check`, and obtain the GPT-6 review the design requires. The wire check does not freeze the design.

A.effort: no reasoning_effort sent; the gateway default, medium per the gateway owner's measurement (PR #423)

B.effort: max, selected by the model alias

harness.runner: promptfoo 0.123.1 HTTP provider (id: http), one provider per arm
harness.prompt: prompt_r02.py:build_prompt, li26 eval_arm.prompt_template(eval_arm.load_plan()) with MARKER replaced once by the filing
harness.transform: transform_r02.js, the gateway's OpenAI chat SSE stream
harness.call_logs: call_logs_by_correlation.py, read-only, six allowlisted columns; each id's rows numbered as attempts and the last marked final (correlation.final_row_rule)
harness.statistics: analyze_r02.py under `uv run --with scipy==1.18.1 --with statsmodels==0.15.0 --with numpy`

request.endpoint_reason: 20128 is the plain gateway; 20129 runs the compression engines and would confound the arms (gateway owner, 2026-09-27)
request.messages: one user message holding li26's prompt with the filing; no system message and no tools, so the gateway's default Codex tool instructions are not added (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1370-1378)
request.stream_options: include_usage true is sent, but the gateway deletes stream_options before the Responses upstream (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts:2912-2916) and attaches usage to the final chunk itself; the transform does not depend on it

response_format.name: li26_filing_items
response_format.derived_from: blueprints/convergence-practice/gpt6-family-tiering-20260926/response.schema.json#/properties/filings/items, with accession removed from properties and required (build_r02.py derive_schema)
response_format.gateway_path: mapped to the Responses text.format with strict kept (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/translator/request/openai-responses/toResponses.ts:35-56), and text passes the codex executor's allowlist (open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1550-1573)

request.schema_sha256_note: sha256 of the derived schema as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces)

headers.Authorization: not sent: the loopback gateway is keyless by the user's decision

request.header_rendering: Nunjucks over the step vars in getHeaders (promptfoo@0.123.1:src/providers/http.ts:2394, 2409); the evaluator adds __evalId, __evalStepId (test-<testIdx>-prompt-<promptIdx>-repeat-<repeatIndex>) and __repeatIndex to them (src/evaluator.ts:744-763, 1646-1653)

not_sent.temperature: none sent; the gateway strips it for codex (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/translator/paramSupport.ts:48 via open-sse/executors/codex/stripPassthroughRejectedParams.ts:13-15, 26; and the codex allowlist, open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1550-1573)
not_sent.top_p: none sent; the gateway strips it for codex (same cites as temperature)
not_sent.seed: none sent; the chat-to-Responses translation builds a new request from named fields and carries no seed (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/translator/request/openai-responses/toResponses.ts:109-113, 432-453), and the codex allowlist has none
not_sent.max_tokens: none sent; for a reasoning model it caps reasoning plus output, so li26's 256 would truncate the max arm, and the gateway deletes it for codex (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1490-1494)
not_sent.reasoning_effort: not sent in either arm; arm B's effort comes from the -max alias, and the codex executor deletes a body reasoning_effort after mapping (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/executors/codex.ts:1488)

subset.algorithm: Stratum = min(number of labelled items, 4). Allocation: largest-remainder proportional allocation of the 60 filings in exact fractions, ties to the lower stratum. Within a stratum, the filings with the smallest sha256('<seed>:<accession>') hex digest. The selection, ordered by (stratum, digest), alternates between the AB run and the BA run, starting with AB. Code: build_r02.py select().

run.order: Two runs with reversed provider lists: promptfooconfig.ab.json on subset.runs.ab and promptfooconfig.ba.json on subset.runs.ba, each with its own __evalId. promptfoo runs each test's repeats in turn and, within one repeat, the providers in config order.
run.promptfoo_cache: --no-cache disables promptfoo's own response cache; X-OmniRoute-No-Cache: true is the gateway's, so both are set

metrics.quality: micro-F1 from TP/FP/FN summed per filing over repeats and then over filings (li26 analyze.micro_f1), never an average of filing F1
metrics.strict_schema_validity: share of calls whose output li26's parse_items marks valid (fenced_valid is scored but is not strict-schema valid)
metrics.cost_per_filing: per arm, mean per call (one call processes one filing once) of reasoning tokens, visible output tokens (completion minus reasoning), completion tokens (reasoning plus output), prompt tokens, uncached input and the cached-input share, from the provider's own usage fields
metrics.absent_usage_details: the gateway writes completion_tokens_details and prompt_tokens_details only when their counts are above 0 (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/translator/response/openai-responses.ts:1403-1419), so on a call that returned usage an absent detail counts as 0; the analysis also reports how many calls carried each detail
metrics.latency: promptfoo latencyMs per call, p50 and p95 (numpy percentile, linear)
metrics.timeouts: calls that failed with promptfoo's 'Request timed out after <ms> ms' (REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, default 300000)
metrics.http_429: per arm: client-side HTTP 429 errors (promptfoo throws before the transform: promptfoo@0.123.1:src/util/fetch/index.ts:681-714, 768-770), call_logs rows with status 429 over all attempts, and final rows with status 429; each call's client-side outcome is cross-tabulated with its final call_logs status. Every call's sent correlation id is rebuilt (correlation.sent_ids), so a client-side 429 and an in-band failure after a slow-path 200 (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/utils/earlyStreamKeepalive.ts:664-685) both join their call_logs rows
metrics.rate_limit_headers: per arm, the calls whose response carried a header named like ratelimit or rate-limit and the names seen (transform metadata.r02.rate_limit_headers), and the calls carrying the gateway's X-OmniRoute-Dropped-Upstream-Headers count; a call promptfoo fails on a remaining count of 0 is the error kind rate_limit_header
metrics.other_errors: transform errors (sse_error_event, malformed_sse_chunks, missing_terminal_chunk, missing_usage, not_an_sse_stream, http_status_<code>) and other provider errors, by kind

effort_measure.primary: client-observed usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens per call, attributable by correlation id; per-filing mean over repeats, arm B minus arm A, with the same paired filing bootstrap (one-sided lower bound) and samples permutation test as quality
effort_measure.zero_reasoning: about 14% of max-effort turns return 0 reasoning tokens as model behaviour (token-save-practice-gpt6's measurement, relayed by the coordinator on 2026-09-27, not measured here), so a per-call zero is not a defect; compare the arms' distributions (mean, median, p95, zero share)
effort_measure.call_logs_columns: secondary check only where non-NULL, on each call's final row (correlation.final_row_rule): reasoning_effort_requested and reasoning_effort_upstream are filled only when the response carried encrypted reasoning (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:src/lib/usage/callLogs.ts:646-653); a NULL is no observation, never 'no effort'. The column allowlist stays exactly the six columns in call_logs_by_correlation.py; request bodies stay off-limits

correlation.header: X-Correlation-Id, set by the caller for every call to the same value as Idempotency-Key (request.headers)
correlation.gateway: a caller X-Correlation-Id is trimmed, has CR/LF removed and is kept when 1-256 characters long (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:292-298, 322; src/shared/utils/correlationPreserve.ts:6-12) as the request id (src/sse/handlers/chat.ts:436), which call_logs stores as correlation_id (src/lib/usage/callLogs.ts:713, 786, 801) and the gateway returns as the X-Correlation-Id response header (src/sse/handlers/chatHelpers.ts:1172-1187; route.ts:313-314)
correlation.sent_ids: analyze_r02.py rebuilds every call's sent id from the results file: evalId, testIdx, promptIdx and the repeat, which is testIdx minus the filing's smallest testIdx. promptfoo renders __evalStepId as test-<testIdx>-prompt-<promptIdx>-repeat-<repeatIndex> and does not persist it (promptfoo@0.123.1:dist/src/evaluator-DlYW7Rgb.js:7599-7619), but every result row keeps testIdx and promptIdx, including a provider error thrown before the transform (:8087-8100, 8133-8157), and a test's repeats take consecutive testIdx values (:8612-8643). `analyze_r02.py ids` refuses to continue when an id the gateway echoed differs from the rebuilt one
correlation.final_row_rule: the gateway writes one call_logs row per attempt under the same correlation id (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/handlers/chatCore/attemptLogging.ts:549-557, 611), stamped with its write time (src/lib/usage/callLogs.ts:680). call_logs_by_correlation.py orders an id's rows by timestamp and then SQLite rowid (insertion order; used only to order, never returned), numbers them as attempts, and marks the last as the call's final row. Status, model and effort per call come from the final row; attempts per call, retried calls and 429 rows count all rows. Several rows for one id are gateway attempts, never separate calls: with maxRetries 0 promptfoo sends one request per result row. The analysis reports a problem when a matched call lacks exactly one final row or its attempts are not numbered 1..n
correlation.unmatched_calls: a sent id with no call_logs row is counted per arm by the call's client-side outcome, never dropped; such calls include requests the gateway rejects before its attempt logging (a peer rejection, or backpressure when OMNI_MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS is set: OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:src/sse/handlers/chat.ts:432-433, 439-442; src/sse/utils/backpressure.ts:25-67). call_logs writes are not awaited (attemptLogging.ts:557, 618; src/lib/usage/callLogs.ts:854-876), so call_logs is read after both runs have finished
correlation.choice: rebuilding the sent ids, over a lookup by the run's evalId prefix: for a completed run the rebuilt ids cover every sent request
correlation.gap: a run that stops before promptfoo writes -o has no results file to rebuild from, and the prefix lookup is not implemented

decision_rule.adopt_max: the one-sided 95% lower bound of micro-F1(B) - micro-F1(A) is above 0
decision_rule.keep_medium: otherwise, when the lower bound of micro-F1(A) - micro-F1(B) is at least -0.02 and A's mean completion (reasoning plus output) tokens per filing are below B's
decision_rule.inconclusive: otherwise; B is not adopted, and neither A's non-inferiority nor its cost advantage is shown
decision_rule.scope: li26 part of R02 only. Memory-role effort is decided on the S3 r6 development runs, and moving a role to cx/gpt-6-sol is outside these two arms

statistics.pairing: by (accession, repeat) across arms; promptfoo gives both arms of one filing and repeat the same testIdx
statistics.unit: filing; per-filing TP/FP/FN summed over repeats

bootstrap.statistic: each filing's two arms are rows of one count table; the samples carry row indices, so a resample moves both arms of a filing together

statistics.multiple_comparisons: statsmodels 0.15.0 multipletests(method='holm') (statsmodels/stats/multitest.py:99) applies only to a family of roles; R02 compares one role, so Holm is not applied
statistics.li26_paired_bootstrap: not reused; scipy's bootstrap replaces it

wire_check.command: PROMPTFOO_CONFIG_DIR=~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/gateway-ab-r02-20260927/promptfoo PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 promptfoo eval -c promptfooconfig.ab.json -t ~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/gateway-ab-r02-20260927/tests-ab.jsonl --filter-first-n 1 --repeat 1 --max-concurrency 1 --no-cache --no-share -o <scratch results.json>
wire_check.configs_note: differ from the committed configs in the description string, which then ended with '; DRAFT, not frozen', and in the X-Correlation-Id header, added afterwards (wire_recheck)
wire_check.outcome: promptfoo exit 0, 2 passed; 2,986 prompt and 77 completion tokens, 37 of them reasoning
wire_check.a_keys: not observed in this check: requestHeaders is absent from both result rows because promptfoo adds it only when context.debug is set (promptfoo@0.123.1:src/providers/http.ts:2734), which eval does not set, and the check's own promptfoo debug log redacts every rendered header value except Content-Type. This was the brief's stop condition; it was reported, not worked around. Resolved by echo_check without a gateway call

b_effort.A: 1 call_logs row by correlation id: status 200, model gpt-6-astra, requested NULL, upstream NULL; no observation
b_effort.B: 1 call_logs row by correlation id: status 200, model gpt-6-astra-max, requested NULL, upstream max; consistent with max

c_usage.placement: usage on the final chunk, which also carries finish_reason stop; [DONE] follows; 9 data chunks per stream, no keepalive frames
c_usage.reading: no prompt_tokens_details in either arm and no completion_tokens_details in arm A, which by the gateway's translator means 0 cached tokens in both and 0 reasoning tokens in A (openai-responses.ts:1403-1419)

wire_check.d_fields: strict json_schema response_format and stream_options returned HTTP 200 in both arms with output {"items":["7.01"]}, parse valid, TP 1; no sampling field was sent, so there was nothing to fix and no re-run; latency A 1780 ms, B 4080 ms; the stream's model field is gpt-6-astra in both arms, the upstream model name (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/translator/response/openai-responses.ts:1016)
wire_check.e_correlation_id: the transform read a non-empty 36-character X-Correlation-Id from each streamed response, distinct across the arms, and copied it into metadata.http.headers and metadata.r02.correlation_id; the persisted results show metadata.http.headers x-correlation-id as [REDACTED] (promptfoo@0.123.1:src/models/evalResult.ts:199-213), so the analysis reads metadata.r02.correlation_id. This id was gateway-generated; the configs now set it (wire_recheck.f_caller_correlation_id)

echo_check.server: go-httpbin v2.25.0 (https://github.com/mccutchen/go-httpbin/releases/tag/v2.25.0), /anything; the linux-amd64 archive matched the release's checksums.txt and the binary matched the archive. Started with -host 127.0.0.1 on a free port and stopped afterwards; it exited and the port was closed
echo_check.configs: generated from the committed configs in a private 0700 directory; a recursive comparison showed they differ only in url (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/anything), transformResponse json, the removed defaultTest, the description and an absolute prompt path
echo_check.url_guard: every providers[*].config.url in both echo configs was exactly the go-httpbin loopback URL, with no :20128 and no omniroute; passed at generation and again immediately before the first eval
echo_check.command: PROMPTFOO_CONFIG_DIR=<private> PROMPTFOO_LOG_DIR=<private> PROMPTFOO_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 promptfoo eval -c <echo config> -t ~/.local/state/native-agent-stack/gateway-ab-r02-20260927/tests-<ab|ba>.jsonl -n 2 --repeat 2 --max-concurrency 1 --no-cache --no-share -o <private>/echo-<ab|ba>.json
echo_check.outcome: each run exited 0 with 8 of 8 passed; go-httpbin logged 16 /anything requests
echo_check.coverage: 2 filings per run, repeats 0 and 1, both provider orders (in the BA run B is prompt column 0)

wire_recheck.outcome: promptfoo exit 0, 2 passed; both outputs parsed valid with TP 1

f_caller_correlation_id.sent_ids: rebuilt from the results, a rebuild echo_check validated, because promptfoo persists no request headers; `analyze_r02.py ids` exited 0
f_caller_correlation_id.call_logs: call_logs_by_correlation.py found exactly the 2 sent ids, 1 row each; 0 retried, 0 unmatched
f_caller_correlation_id.A: status 200, model gpt-6-astra, requested NULL, upstream NULL; no observation
f_caller_correlation_id.B: status 200, model gpt-6-astra-max, requested NULL, upstream max; consistent with max

A.reasoning_tokens: no detail (0 by the gateway's translator)

q3_rate_limit_headers.source: on a fast-path stream the gateway forwards upstream headers whose names contain ratelimit or rate-limit at priority 2, after request and correlation ids and Retry-After, within a 768-byte budget, and reports how many it dropped in X-OmniRoute-Dropped-Upstream-Headers (OmniRoute@dd6e9607e:open-sse/handlers/chatCore/responseHeaders.ts:49-51, 133-163, 245-352); a slow-path stream commits the keepalive wrapper's headers only (open-sse/utils/earlyStreamKeepalive.ts:21-31, 720-728)
q3_rate_limit_headers.observed: no rate-limit-class header on either call
q3_rate_limit_headers.B: fast path: only the handler's streaming headers carry the dropped-header count (responseHeaders.ts:337-339; open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingResponseHeaders.ts:34), and B's reported 10 upstream headers dropped over the budget; which headers were forwarded or dropped is not recorded
q3_rate_limit_headers.A: no dropped-header count; its stream began with a keepalive chunk, which is the slow-path startup frame (earlyStreamKeepalive.ts:43-48; src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:307-316) or the stream pipeline's heartbeat (open-sse/utils/sseHeartbeat.ts:62-70; open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingPipeline.ts:111-117). At the default 15 s heartbeat interval (src/shared/utils/runtimeTimeouts.ts:23) a 1010 ms call can only have received the startup frame, so A most likely took the slow path; the host's configured interval was not read
q3_rate_limit_headers.scope: two calls on one host and day; not evidence that the upstream never sends such headers or that a forwarded one could never read 0

post_run.call_logs: python3 call_logs_by_correlation.py ~/.local/share/omniroute/storage.sqlite <ids.json> --rows > <private call-logs.json>, after both runs have finished, with ids.json from `analyze_r02.py ids` (the rebuilt sent id of every call)
post_run.gateway_owner_handoff: send each arm's correlation ids with the run window, arm tags (r02-A, r02-B) and key prefixes (r02-a-, r02-b-); the owner returns per arm the call count, distinct accounts and per-account call counts under masked labels shared across arms, call_logs status counts including 429, and any unmatched ids, plus a masked per-arm account-balance read. No connection or account ids are retained

limitations: The account behind each call is an uncontrolled factor: per-conversation session keys spread calls across the gateway's 4 accounts, and no account column is read here; the gateway owner supplies the masked per-arm distribution after the run.
li26 is near ceiling for GPT-6 (0.992-0.995 for every tier, #359 and #397), so a quality difference is unlikely to be detectable; this is a cost and wire test with a non-inferiority bound.

A call the gateway rejects before its attempt logging has no call_logs row; it is counted as unmatched by its client-side outcome (correlation.unmatched_calls). A run that stops before promptfoo writes -o cannot have its sent ids rebuilt (correlation.gap).

A 200 response carrying x-ratelimit-remaining-requests, x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens or X-RateLimit-Remaining equal to 0 is treated by promptfoo as rate limited and, with maxRetries 0, fails (promptfoo@0.123.1:src/util/fetch/index.ts:375-388, 712-714; installed dist/src/fetch-DpK1Rb6J.js:1200-1204, 1432-1453, 1464-1495). The gateway forwards rate-limit-class upstream headers on fast-path streams within its budget, and the re-check saw none on its 2 calls (wire_recheck.q3_rate_limit_headers). Such a failure is the error kind rate_limit_header, and call_logs still shows the gateway's side of the call through its rebuilt id.
Other clients (hindsight-live, cognee-live) call cx/gpt-6-astra-max through the same gateway, so call_logs is read by correlation id, never by window and model.
call_logs effort columns stay NULL without encrypted reasoning, so arm A's medium effort is not directly observable here; the gateway owner's PR #423 is the evidence for it.

open_questions.1_correlation_id: answered: the caller X-Correlation-Id is kept, returned and stored as call_logs.correlation_id (wire_recheck.f_caller_correlation_id)
open_questions.2_rows_per_id: partly answered from source: one row per attempt under the same id, handled by correlation.final_row_rule; open: does the gateway retry an upstream 429 on another account?
open_questions.3_rate_limit_headers: partly answered: forwarded on fast-path streams within a 768-byte budget, none seen on 2 calls (wire_recheck.q3_rate_limit_headers); open: does the Codex upstream send x-ratelimit-remaining-* at all, and can they survive the budget next to the Codex quota headers of the same priority?
open_questions.4_arm_a_effort: open: an observation of arm A's effective effort that does not depend on encrypted reasoning, besides PR #423
